subject: Streaming edge cases, measurement approach and SLA language (CuraHealth)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Avery Rossi <avery.rossi@curahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Streaming edge cases & measurement — post-call recap

Hi Avery,

Great to connect this morning. Quick recap of the performance requirements you confirmed and the open items we promised to follow up on: 

Summary of requirements you validated
- Use case: real-time clinical transcription + incremental summarization for clinician dashboard.
- End-to-end perceived latency target: 95% of streaming sessions should see first actionable token within 350ms.
- Per-chunk (stream delta) behavior: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 180ms for subsequent tokens under normal load.
- Concurrency: typical production concurrency ~60 live sessions, sustained load up to 500 requests/minute with bursts to 1,200 req/min for <5 minutes.
- Throughput sensitivity: heavy tail on a small percent of sessions (large transcripts up to 8k tokens) — need graceful degradation.
- Consistency: maintain ordering and no dropped chunks for in-flight KV cache lookups.

Open items we agreed to follow up on
1) Measurement method: how Redwood will measure p50/p95 (synthetic probes vs customer telemetry vs agent-side traces).
2) Exclusions: confirm maintenance windows and traffic-override events that should be excluded from SLO calculations.
3) Reporting cadence and dashboards: monthly report + incident drilldown within 48 hours of any P95 breach.
4) Remedies language: draft of credit calculation and remediation steps (rollback to a compatible variant, automated fallback).
5) Sample traffic profile: you mentioned sharing a sample capture — please attach the traffic profile (we saw one come through after our call).

Next steps from Redwood
- Neha will outline a recommended measurement approach and sample test harness (synthetic probes from two regions + replay of your sample capture).
- I will circulate proposed SLA wording and a short playbook for exclusion handling and remedies for legal and ops review.
- If the attached sample traffic (cura_traffic_profile.json) looks right, we will run a focused qualification pass against a representative model variant and share the telemetry.

If that aligns with your notes, we’ll prepare a concise SLA patch you can pass to procurement.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

--
Attachment: cura_traffic_profile.json (application/json) - sample request traces from CuraHealth test environment

From: Avery Rossi <avery.rossi@curahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@curahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-25T10:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming edge cases & measurement — post-call recap

Jordan — thanks for the tidy recap, that's exactly what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side before you draft the SLA patch: 

1) First-token: the 350ms is a hard requirement for clinician-facing real-time alerts. For batch-style summaries it's less strict. Please mark which SLOs are session-type specific.
2) Burst behavior: when we say "bursts to 1,200 req/min", that is typically concentrated to a single region for a few minutes — if you need, we can provide tags in the sample profile that mark those burst windows.
3) Exclusions: any customer-originated misconfiguration (e.g., malformed payloads, duplicated requests) should be excluded. Planned maintenance windows must be mutually agreed and published at least 48 hours in advance.
4) Remedies: acceptable initial approach is tiered credits and an automated rollback to the last known-good model variant if a P95 breach is sustained for >15 minutes. We expect a clear notification path for ops.

Please go ahead and share the SLA wording and the sample test harness details. We'll loop in procurement after we see the proposed remedies.

Avery Rossi
Head of Platform Integrations | CuraHealth
avery.rossi@curahealth.com

--
Forwarded attachment included: cura_traffic_profile.json (contains synthetic + production-like replay samples).

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming edge cases & measurement — proposal for metrics & exclusions

Folks,

Based on the call notes and Avery's clarification, I drafted an internal proposal for how we measure the streaming SLOs and the exclusion list. Below is the condensed version I recommend we include in the SLA patch. I also attached a CSV with QPS profiles from our last qualification run.

Proposed measurement approach (for inclusion in contract):
- Primary metric: two-part measurement
  a) Time-to-first-token (TTFT): measured at Redwood edge from request acceptance to first byte of generated token visible to client. Use P95 computed across production traffic windows, sampled hourly and aggregated monthly.
  b) Streaming delta: measured as per-token inter-arrival time (client-observed delta between chunk boundaries) — compute p50 and p95 across per-session token deltas.
- Sources: prefer Redwood synthetic probes + customer telemetry if provided. For contractual measurement, Redwood's edge telemetry is the authoritative source; customer-provided traces used for validation.

Exclusions (contract language):
- Scheduled maintenance windows mutually agreed and posted >=48 hours in advance.
- Customer-originated malformed payloads, authentication failures, or rate-limited requests listed in client's dashboard.
- Upstream provider outages (e.g., cloud region outage) when not caused by Redwood's routing.
- Traffic spikes that exceed a mutually-agreed burst profile (we'll include CuraHealth's burst tags).

Reporting & remedies
- Monthly SLA report delivered within 5 business days of month end.
- Incident report within 48 hours for any P95 breach lasting >15 minutes.
- Remedies: credits calculated as percentage of monthly Redwood fees tied to the affected product (0-10% per incident tiered by duration/severity), plus recommended automatic rollback to the prior model variant as a mitigation step.

Next immediate actions
1) Jordan: include this language in the draft SLA document for procurement review.
2) Ben: can you validate the proposed credit bands vs standard Redwood commercial practice?
3) I'll prepare the qualification test harness plan (synthetic + replay) and an initial runbook for ops to exercise fallback behaviors.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

--
Attachment: qps_profile.csv (text/csv) - representative qps and burst markers

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Avery Rossi <avery.rossi@curahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, platform@curahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-25T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Draft SLA patch + next steps (attached)

Avery — attaching the initial SLA patch (proposed_sla_patch.docx) that incorporates Neha's measurement language and the exclusions we discussed. High level changes: 

- Explicit TTFT and streaming-delta metrics with measurement definitions (Redwood edge telemetry as authoritative).
- Exclusion list per Neha's recommendations plus a short section on customer-side instrumented telemetry.
- Reporting cadence: monthly + 48-hour incident summaries.
- Remedies: tiered credit bands plus automated rollback playbook.

Please review the attached and let me know any redlines procurement wants. For our side: Ben, can you confirm the credit band numbers we can commit to for an initial pilot? Legal will want final wording, but this draft should be sufficient for procurement to proceed to the next internal step.

Proposed timeline
- This week: Redwood and Cura ops agree on maintenance windows and final burst tag schema.
- Early next week: Redwood runs a representative qualification pass using the provided cura_traffic_profile.json and shares telemetry.
- By 2026-12-03: procurement draft signed off for pilot.

Thanks again — attaching: proposed_sla_patch.docx and a copy of cura_traffic_profile.json for traceability.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
